title: SSE connection bootstrapping and micro-burst delta-coalescing adapter
creator: Marcos Rivera
description: Add a negotiated bootstrap handshake and server-side micro-burst delta-coalescing adapter for SSE clients. The goal is to reduce per-event overhead during short high-frequency bursts while preserving ordered, idempotent reassembly and backwards compatibility with existing JSONL/legacy SSE clients.
acceptance_criteria: Server advertises capability bits and suggested coalescing window in initial HTTP response headers and in the first SSE meta event.
Clients that opt-in receive coalesced delta frames during micro-bursts; clients that do not opt-in see unchanged JSONL stream behavior.
Reconnects use a monotonic resume-seq token with a checksum; server can synthesize idempotent replays that never duplicate application-visible tool/function-call boundaries.
End-to-end test harness shows >=35% reduction in per-token request cost for micro-burst workload (bursts: 50-500 events in <2s) without increasing 99th percentile latency beyond SLO thresholds.
No regressions in existing streaming integrations (console, SDKs) verified by integration tests and canary telemetry.
design_notes: Introduce 'Redwood-Stream-Capabilities' initial header: comma-separated tokens (resume-v2, coalesce-ms=30, checksum=sha256, jsonl-compat).

Handshake consists of: initial HTTP 200 + headers, then a dedicated SSE meta event 'redwood.handshake' containing the same capabilities as JSON so proxies that strip headers can still learn capabilities.

Coalescing adapter groups contiguous small delta events within a sliding window (default 30ms, configurable per-client). Each coalesced frame includes an ordered vector of deltas and a frame-level checksum and sequence range.
Resume token becomes monotonic pair: <session-id>:<last-seq>-<commit-checksum>. Server keeps short lived commit logs to enable gap-filling on reconnect without re-emitting full model outputs.
Tool/function-call boundary guarantee: coalescing cannot fold across an explicit function_call sentinel; adapter ensures atomicity of any function_call payloads.
Fallback rules: If client indicates 'jsonl-compat' only, server will not coalesce and will preserve existing newline-delimited chunk framing.
Metrics to add: coalesced_frame_rate, avg_coalesce_window_ms, resumed_gap_fill_count, coalescing_cpu_ns, percent_messages_coalesced.
Security: handshake header cannot be used to escalate privileges; resume tokens are short-lived and tied to tenant scope.
Compatibility: behavior must be spec-compatible with lightweight HTTP/2 eventstream proxies; include meta-event for header-poor environments.
implementation_plan: (Backend) Add handshake header parsing in streaming ingress and emit 'redwood.handshake' meta event in first SSE payload. (Priya)
(Runtime) Implement coalescing adapter module: event buffer, window timer, checksum computation, and safe flush semantics respecting function_call sentinels. (Backend team)
(Storage) Short-term commit log: ring buffer per-session for last N frames (configurable, default 128) to enable limited gap fill on reconnect. (Infra)
(API) Extend SDKs: add opt-in flag `streamCoalesce: true` and resume token handling helpers. (SDKs)
(Telemetry) Wire new metrics and trace spans. Add dashboards and alert thresholds. (Observability)
(Tests) Unit tests for ordering/idempotency, property tests for duplicates/loss/reordering, and e2e harness validating cost/latency for burst patterns. (QA)
Create PRs: small modular changes with feature flag `stream.coalesce.enabled`. Plan for gradual rollout.
testing_plan: Unit: adapter state machine correctness, checksum mismatch handling, function_call atomicity invariant.
Property: simulate network loss, duplicates, reorder up to 100ms and assert final reassembled sequence equals authoritative log.
Integration: SDK opt-in test matrix (node, python, go) against canary server with and without coalescing.
Load: micro-burst workload generator (50-500 events in 0.5-2s) measuring token cost, 50/95/99 latencies, coalesce ratio.
Backward-compat: run legacy clients that only support JSONL and confirm no behavioral changes.
Security: fuzz header parsing and resume token validation; verify no cross-tenant leakage by token misuse tests.
rollout_plan: Enable for internal dev clusters + SDK beta builds for 48 hours.
Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 72h -> monitor errors, resumed_gap_fill_count, latencies -> 10% for 72h.
If metrics stable, increase to 50% then full rollout over 7 days.
Provide quick rollback by disabling feature flag and expiring coalesce windows gracefully (flush on disable).
risks: Coalescing may increase P99 latency for rare synchronous streaming flows — mitigate with per-route coalesce disable.
Resume gap-fill complexity: storage ring buffer needs mem/CPU budget; misconfiguration could cause failed resumes.
Proxies that strip headers require robust meta-event fallback; missing this could lead to client/server capability mismatch.
Function_call boundary correctness is critical; bug could create API-visible duplication or truncated tool calls.
